models_evaluated: 6 LLMs from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI (specific model names not given in abstract)

links.outcome: Recall on undeterminable cases (whether LLMs withhold judgment) versus eligible/ineligible cases
links.effect: Eligible/ineligible recall 86.5%-98.6%; undeterminable recall 44.6%-70.3%; information gap-filling was 83.4% of 235 errors, and undeterminable cases were mostly misclassified as eligible.
links.quote: Eligible and ineligible cases were classified with high recall (86.5%-98.6%), but undeterminable cases showed a marked decline across all models (44.6%-70.3%).

unlisted_practices: Tristate adjudication framework (eligible/ineligible/undeterminable) for logic-based error analysis of LLM reimbursement decisions
Structure-guided prompting for eligibility reasoning (no significant change from baseline)
Converting guideline documents to structured text as LLM input (degraded performance)
Enabling web search tools for LLM eligibility verification (0%-3.2% tool invocation, no significant change)

screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark for anticancer reimbursement eligibility determination using LLMs and conducts sensitivity analyses testing prompt/input strategies (structured text conversion, structure-guided prompting, and web search integration) against baseline performance.

primary.practice: structure-guided prompting and web search integration
